intended_use: Flags individual card transactions that look potentially fraudulent so the payments risk team can review them before settlement. It is a triage aid that produces a queue for human reviewers, not an automated block on the customer's card.
training_data: Trained on the card_activity feature group from Week 4 (raw source card_activity_features_v1): historical card transactions labelled fraud / not-fraud. Coverage is limited to the transaction activity captured in that group - it has no merchant-category, device, or geolocation features and carries whatever sampling and label-lag bias exists in the upstream source.
limitations: The model is a single amount-threshold rule, so it can only separate 'large' from 'small' transactions. It structurally cannot catch low-value fraud, card-testing micro-charges, or fraud that is deliberately split into several sub-threshold payments, and it will flag every legitimate high-value purchase as suspicious.
ethical_considerations: A false positive delays or blocks a legitimate purchase and inconveniences the customer; a false negative lets fraud through and the monetary loss falls on the business and the customer's time to dispute it. Because amount is the only feature, customers who routinely make large legitimate purchases absorb a disproportionate share of the false positives.
